title: Punch Out on Ambiguous or Invalid Workflow Handoffs

story.so_that: uncertain or invalid intermediate results never advance silently through story analysis
story.i_want: every activity handoff validated and ambiguous failures routed to a controlled human decision

journey.before: Configures and starts a story analysis workflow, monitors activity outputs, and expects guardrails to catch invalid or ambiguous intermediate artifacts before they propagate.
journey.during: Reviews handoff validation outcomes, receives ambiguity escalations, and issues retry, accept, or abort decisions through the trusted operator path when the workflow enters an awaiting_signal state.
journey.after: Confirms that downstream activities never consume invalid artifacts, that valid bounded decisions resolve punch-outs, and that every guardrail and human decision is recorded for audit.

capability_breakdown.core_action: Validate every inter-activity handoff in the story analysis workflow and route ambiguous or invalid outcomes to a durable human decision.
inputs: Expected JSON Schema for the artifact
Explicit ambiguity result from an activity or guardrail
Human decision signal (retry, accept, or abort) through the trusted operator path
Configured timeout policy for unresolved punch-outs
outputs: Dependent activity scheduled exactly once for valid handoffs
Automated guardrail failure record naming the step and failed rule
awaiting_signal workflow state with reason ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY
Bounded retry, human-resolved, or human-aborted terminal path
Guardrail outcome, escalation reason, decision, decision origin, and terminal path logged
state_changes: Workflow advances to the dependent activity when a handoff guardrail passes
Workflow records an automated guardrail failure and does not advance when an artifact is missing, unreadable, or schema-invalid
Workflow enters awaiting_signal when an activity or guardrail reports an explicit ambiguous outcome
Workflow transitions to a bounded retry, human-resolved, or human-aborted terminal path after a valid decision
Workflow applies the documented bounded timeout policy and logs the outcome when no valid decision arrives in time
Concurrent runs and retries remain isolated so only the current run and attempt artifact is accepted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a completed activity points to an existing readable artifact that matches the expected schema, when the handoff guardrail runs, then the dependent activity is scheduled exactly once.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a completed activity points to an existing readable artifact that matches the expected schema When the handoff guardrail runs Then the dependent activity is scheduled exactly once

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an activity output path is missing, nonexistent, a directory, or unreadable, when the handoff guardrail runs, then the dependent activity is not scheduled and the workflow records an automated guardrail failure naming the step and failed rule.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an activity output path is missing, nonexistent, a directory, or unreadable When the handoff guardrail runs Then the dependent activity is not scheduled and the workflow records an automated guardrail failure naming the step and failed rule

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an activity artifact is malformed JSON or violates its expected schema, when the handoff guardrail runs, then the dependent activity is not scheduled and the workflow records an automated guardrail failure.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an activity artifact is malformed JSON or violates its expected schema When the handoff guardrail runs Then the dependent activity is not scheduled and the workflow records an automated guardrail failure

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the grader passes, when the post-grader guardrail runs, then it confirms the intent, analysis, and analysis-grade artifacts all exist and match their schemas before the workflow can complete successfully.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given the grader passes When the post-grader guardrail runs Then it confirms the intent, analysis, and analysis-grade artifacts all exist and match their schemas before the workflow completes successfully

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given concurrent workflows or retries produce similarly named artifacts, when a handoff is validated, then only the artifact associated with the current workflow run and activity attempt is accepted.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given concurrent workflows or retries produce similarly named artifacts When a handoff is validated Then only the artifact associated with the current workflow run and activity attempt is accepted
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Accept only the current attempt's artifact

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an activity or guardrail explicitly reports an ambiguous outcome, when the engine evaluates it, then the workflow enters awaiting_signal with reason ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY and does not schedule the next activity.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an activity or guardrail explicitly reports an ambiguous outcome When the engine evaluates it Then the workflow enters awaiting_signal with reason ACTIVITY_FLAGGED_AMBIGUITY and does not schedule the next activity

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workflow awaits an ambiguity decision, when a supported retry decision is received through the trusted operator path, then the bounded retry transition occurs once and is logged.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow awaits an ambiguity decision When a supported retry decision is received through the trusted operator path Then the bounded retry transition occurs once and is logged
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Retry flagged activities via trusted signal

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workflow awaits an ambiguity decision, when a supported accept or abort decision is received through the trusted operator path, then the corresponding human-resolved or human-aborted terminal path occurs once and is logged distinctly from automated failure.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow awaits an ambiguity decision When a supported accept or abort decision is received through the trusted operator path Then the corresponding human-resolved or human-aborted terminal path occurs once and is logged distinctly from automated failure
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Resolve ambiguity with accept or abort

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a workflow awaits a decision, when an unsupported, stale, duplicate, or out-of-state decision is sent, then it does not advance or overwrite the workflow's valid state.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a workflow awaits a decision When an unsupported, stale, duplicate, or out-of-state decision is sent Then the workflow does not advance or overwrite its valid state

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given no valid decision arrives before the configured timeout, when timeout handling completes, then the documented bounded timeout policy is applied once and the outcome is logged.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given no valid decision arrives before the configured timeout When timeout handling completes Then the documented bounded timeout policy is applied once and the outcome is logged
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Apply timeout policy to unresolved punch-outs

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An integration or end-to-end test sends an invalid decision to a live awaiting workflow and proves that the wait cannot be bypassed.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an integration or end-to-end test sends an invalid decision to a live awaiting workflow Then the test proves the wait cannot be bypassed
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Certify ambiguity wait cannot be bypassed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At least one recorded workflow run demonstrates the full ambiguity path from flagged result through a valid human decision.
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a recorded workflow run demonstrates the full ambiguity path When it is inspected Then it shows the path from flagged result through a valid human decision
